title: US Sen. Cantwell releases framework for 'safe and secure' frontier AI
key_facts: Maria Cantwell, Democratic ranking member of the Senate Commerce Committee, released a six-point framework for AI regulation on Wednesday 7 Oct 2026.
The framework does not include legislative text.
It would have the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) set standards for frontier AI models, including ways to address catastrophic risks such as loss of control.
Models under those standards would need continuous testing by government and third-party groups, and independent audits would confirm compliance.
Frontier developers would publicly disclose potential risks and report safety incidents.
The enforcement mechanism is not yet decided; a committee aide said it could include civil or criminal penalties.
The framework contrasts with a focus from the White House and some congressional Republicans on voluntary standards and self-regulation.
quote_evidence: "To manage risks from advanced AI systems we need clear safety standards, continuous testing, and reporting of serious failures," Cantwell said in a statement Wednesday.
The six-point framework, which does not include legislative text, stands in contrast to a focus from the White House and some congressional Republicans on voluntary standards and self-regulation.
why_it_matters_hint: A minority-party plan for federal safety testing of the most powerful AI models; no bill text yet.
